thag16.8:1.1:
Aṅgulimāla:
“While walking, contemplative,
you say, ’I have stopped.’
thag16.8:1.2:
But when I have stopped
you say that I haven’t.
thag16.8:1.3: I ask you the meaning of this:
thag16.8:1.4:
How have you stopped?
How haven’t I?”
thag16.8:2.1:
The Buddha:
“I have stopped, Aṅgulimāla,
once & for all,
thag16.8:2.2:
having cast off violence
toward all living beings.
thag16.8:2.3:
You, though,
are unrestrained toward beings.
thag16.8:2.4:
That’s how I’ve stopped
and you haven’t.”
thag16.8:3.1:
Aṅgulimāla:
“At long last a greatly revered great seer
thag16.8:3.2:
for my sake
has come to the great forest.
thag16.8:3.3:
Having heard your verse
in line with the Dhamma,
thag16.8:3.4:
I will go about
having abandoned evil.”
thag16.8:4.1:
So saying, the bandit
hurled his sword & weapons
thag16.8:4.2:
over a cliff
into a chasm,
a pit.
thag16.8:4.3:
Then the bandit paid homage
to the feet of the One Well-Gone,
thag16.8:4.4: and right there requested the Going-forth.
thag16.8:5.1:
The Awakened One,
the compassionate great seer,
thag16.8:5.2: the teacher of the world, along with its devas,
thag16.8:5.4:
That in itself
was monkhood for him.
thag16.8:6.4: like the moon set free from a cloud.
thag16.8:7.4: like the moon set free from a cloud.
thag16.8:8.2:
devotes himself
to the Buddha’s bidding:
thag16.8:8.4: like the moon set free from a cloud.
thag16.8:9.1:
May even my enemies
hear talk of the Dhamma.
thag16.8:9.2:
May even my enemies
devote themselves
to the Buddha’s bidding.
thag16.8:9.3:
May even my enemies
associate with those people
who—peaceful, good—
thag16.8:9.4: get others to accept the Dhamma.
thag16.8:10.1:
May even my enemies
hear the Dhamma time & again
thag16.8:10.2:
from those who advise endurance,
forbearance,
thag16.8:11.1: For surely he wouldn’t harm me,
thag16.8:11.3: he would attain the foremost peace,
thag16.8:13.1: Some tame with a blunt stick,
thag16.8:13.3: But without blunt or bladed weapons
thag16.8:13.4: I was tamed by the one who is Such.
thag16.8:14.1: “Doer of No Harm” is my name,
thag16.8:14.2: but I used to be a doer of harm.
thag16.8:14.3: Today I am true to my name,
thag16.8:14.4: for I harm no one at all.
thag16.8:15.1:
A bandit
I used to be,
thag16.8:15.3: Swept along by a great flood,
thag16.8:15.4: I went to the Buddha as refuge.
thag16.8:16.4:
Uprooted is [craving],
the guide to becoming.
thag16.8:17.1: Having done the type of kamma
thag16.8:17.2:
that would lead to many
bad destinations,
thag16.8:17.3: touched by the fruit of [that] kamma,
thag16.8:18.3:
while one who is wise
cherishes heedfulness
thag16.8:19.2:
or to intimacy
with sensual delight—
thag16.8:19.3:
for a heedful person,
absorbed in jhāna,
thag16.8:20.1: This has come well & not gone away,
thag16.8:20.2: it was not badly thought through for me.
thag16.8:21.1: This has come well & not gone away,
thag16.8:21.2: it was not badly thought through for me.
thag16.8:21.3:
The three knowledges
have been attained;
thag16.8:22.1:
Where once I stayed here & there
with shuddering mind—
thag16.8:22.2:
in the wilderness,
at the foot of a tree,
thag16.8:23.1: with ease I now lie down, I stand,
thag16.8:23.2: with ease I live my life.
thag16.8:23.4: O, the Teacher has shown me sympathy!
thag16.8:24.1: Before, I was of brahman stock,
thag16.8:24.3:
Today I’m the son
of the One Well-Gone,
thag16.8:25.1: Rid of craving, devoid of clinging,
thag16.8:25.3: having killed the root of evil,
thag16.8:25.4: I’ve reached the end of the effluents.
thag16.8:26.1: The Teacher has been served by me;
